who: claude-fable-5-2 (Claude Fable 5.2), main agent, lane proofs-1113
task: Prove a property of code that shares atomics between two threads (a park and its unpark, a flag and its reader, a lock word) for every interleaving, with the clock where time matters, in place of a simulation test that draws schedules
do: 1. The core imports its atomics from `blaze_core::atomic` (std's outside blaze-core's tests, the scheduled ones in them). 2. State each claim as a function of a schedule: `fn name(schedule: Vec<threads::Step>, ..) -> bool` that makes the shared atomics, runs the two real functions as closures with `blaze_core::world::threads::two(&schedule, || a(..), || b(..))`, and says what must hold of how each thread stood (`Ended::Done(v)`, `Running`, `Asleep`). A lost wakeup is `(Asleep, Done)`. A schedule that ends before a thread does says nothing of it. For time: `threads::clock(&readings)` before the run, the core's clock is `threads::now()`, its kernel wait `threads::wait_until(word, expected, deadline)`, and `threads::time()` after the run is the clock; time moves only where someone looks. Orderings weaker than `SeqCst` over more than one word: `threads::two_weak` (decision D46; its statements are not translated yet). 3. Read the simulation test's oracle clause by clause and give each clause a theorem before deleting the test: the park needed four (no unpark is lost; never early and not asleep past the deadline; left alone it returns or sleeps within N steps; ready exactly for a token), and the last was found only by that reading. 4. Run each where it is stated: a `blaze_sim::check` test that draws schedules, readings and deadlines with `must_reach` for each way the run ends, and one control per clause (a planted kernel behind the core's trait, or the oracle given a start its claim does not match). 5. Bound what the model bounds: a `Vec` holds `usize::MAX` elements and `push` panics past it, so a statement that pushes says nothing of a schedule with no room (the first promptness statement was false for that). 6. `blaze prove -p <crate>` emits the models (each function that reaches an atomic is a `Threads.Prog` whose program points are the definitions `f.at_n` and `f.loop_k.at_n`); copy the new ones under `lean/BlazeModel/` and run `lake build BlazeModel` (H-proof-loop). A theorem with no proof makes `blaze prove` exit 1: keep its attribute off main until it is proved. 7. The proof, by an Opus lane to an exact brief (the statement, the files to read, the plan, one check command): points and shapes from the model's own named definitions (`BlazeCore/Wait/ParkingTimeLib.lean`), the table of reachable states (`Good` in `ParkingTime.lean`: both points, the word, who sleeps, who is woken; the clock only where a claim needs it), one step lemma per thread (`Advance.of_step` with the `World.step_*` lemma of the operation), then `two_ends` for every schedule, `two_exec_append` for a schedule in two parts, `two_exec_alone` and `two_exec_first` for one thread alone (`lean/Blaze/ThreadsAuto.lean`). Split a lane's work so it never waits: the theorem about the run needs only the park's and unpark's models; the last step needs the statement's own model. 8. Check it yourself: `lake build` of the proof file's module, a scratch file that prints `#print axioms` (only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound) and checks `(name.spec.proof : name.spec.statement)`, then `blaze prove` on the exact tree.
why: On 2026-11-14 the park's four theorems were proved of the real `park` and `unpark` this way (31 reachable states on the timed kernel, each proof 10 to 20 minutes of a lane once its statement and plan were exact), and its simulation test through the core was deleted. Supersedes H-prove-two-threads, whose step 5 copied the model's continuations by hand (models name their points since #2153) and which had no clock.
